Compute the Identity by State Matrix for a gen_tibble object

Source: R/pairwise_ibs.R
pairwise_ibs.Rd

This function computes the IBS matrix.

Usage

pairwise_ibs(
  x,
  as_matrix = FALSE,
  type = c("proportion", "adjusted_counts", "raw_counts"),
  block_size = bigstatsr::block_size(nrow(x)),
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores()
)

Arguments

x

a gen_tibble object.

as_matrix

boolean, determining whether the results should be a square symmetrical matrix (TRUE), or a tidied tibble (FALSE, the default)

type

one of:

  • "proportion" (the default): the proportion of alleles that are identical by state, a similarity (as --distance ibs flat-missing in PLINK, which writes it to a .mibs file).

  • "adjusted_counts": the allele count distance, a dissimilarity (as --distance flat-missing in PLINK, which writes it to a .dist file): the number of alleles that differ between two individuals, scaled up by the number of loci over the number of loci genotyped in both individuals, to correct for missing genotypes. It equals 2 * n_loci * (1 - proportion), so it is 0 for identical individuals and at most 2 * n_loci. PLINK's default correction for missing genotypes (without flat-missing) is not available (see Details).

  • "raw_counts": the counts of identical alleles and of non-missing alleles, from which the two other quantities are computed.

block_size

maximum number of loci read at once. Genotypes are compared in a compact bit-packed form, so this has little effect on memory use.

n_cores

number of cores to be used, it defaults to bigstatsr::nb_cores()

Value

for "proportion" and "adjusted_counts", a tidy tibble with one row per pair of individuals (columns item1, item2 and value), or a square matrix if as_matrix = TRUE; for "raw_counts", a list of two bigstatsr::FBM matrices, ibs (the counts of alleles identical by state) and valid_n (the counts of non-missing alleles, i.e. twice the number of loci genotyped in both individuals).

Details

Note that monomorphic sites are currently considered (as in PLINK). Remove monomorphic sites before running pairwise_ibs() if this is a concern.

Imputed genotypes are used if x is set to use them (see gt_set_imputed()), and treated as missing otherwise.

Missing genotypes are handled as in PLINK with the flat-missing modifier (--distance ibs flat-missing for "proportion", --distance flat-missing for "adjusted_counts"): each pair of individuals is compared only on the loci genotyped in both, and all loci have the same weight. By default (without flat-missing), PLINK 1.9 instead divides each distance by one minus the sum of the average contributions to the distance of the loci missing in the pair, which depend on their allele frequencies. This default correction is not available in pairwise_ibs(), so, when genotypes are missing, its values are only comparable to those of PLINK run with flat-missing. Without missing genotypes, both corrections give the same values.

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("gen_tbl")

pairwise_ibs(example_gt, type = "proportion")
#> # A tibble: 21 × 3
#>    item1 item2 value
#>    <chr> <chr> <dbl>
#>  1 a     b     0.8  
#>  2 a     c     0.7  
#>  3 a     d     0.833
#>  4 a     e     0.75 
#>  5 a     f     0.6  
#>  6 a     g     0.7  
#>  7 b     c     0.75 
#>  8 b     d     0.8  
#>  9 b     e     0.5  
#> 10 b     f     0.5  
#> # ℹ 11 more rows

# Alternatively, return a matrix
pairwise_ibs(example_gt, type = "proportion", as_matrix = TRUE)
#>           a    b     c         d         e    f     g
#> a 1.0000000 0.80 0.700 0.8333333 0.7500000 0.60 0.700
#> b 0.8000000 1.00 0.750 0.8000000 0.5000000 0.50 0.500
#> c 0.7000000 0.75 1.000 0.6000000 0.7000000 0.75 0.625
#> d 0.8333333 0.80 0.600 1.0000000 0.5833333 0.70 0.500
#> e 0.7500000 0.50 0.700 0.5833333 1.0000000 0.60 0.500
#> f 0.6000000 0.50 0.750 0.7000000 0.6000000 1.00 0.750
#> g 0.7000000 0.50 0.625 0.5000000 0.5000000 0.75 1.000
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "pairwise_matrix" "matrix"          "array"          

# Adjust block_size
pairwise_ibs(example_gt, block_size = 2)
#> # A tibble: 21 × 3
#>    item1 item2 value
#>    <chr> <chr> <dbl>
#>  1 a     b     0.8  
#>  2 a     c     0.7  
#>  3 a     d     0.833
#>  4 a     e     0.75 
#>  5 a     f     0.6  
#>  6 a     g     0.7  
#>  7 b     c     0.75 
#>  8 b     d     0.8  
#>  9 b     e     0.5  
#> 10 b     f     0.5  
#> # ℹ 11 more rows

# Change type
pairwise_ibs(example_gt, type = "adjusted_counts")
#> # A tibble: 21 × 3
#>    item1 item2 value
#>    <chr> <chr> <dbl>
#>  1 a     b       2.4
#>  2 a     c       3.6
#>  3 a     d       2  
#>  4 a     e       3  
#>  5 a     f       4.8
#>  6 a     g       3.6
#>  7 b     c       3  
#>  8 b     d       2.4
#>  9 b     e       6  
#> 10 b     f       6  
#> # ℹ 11 more rows
pairwise_ibs(example_gt, type = "raw_counts")
#> $ibs
#> A Filebacked Big Matrix of type 'double' with 7 rows and 7 columns.
#> 
#> $valid_n
#> A Filebacked Big Matrix of type 'double' with 7 rows and 7 columns.
#>
